Fáilte Ireland invites applications for the position of Support, Product and Regional Development Wild Atlantic Way. Reporting to the Manager, Product and Regional Development Wild Atlantic Way, the successful candidate will provide administrative and operational support to the team, helping to deliver destination development initiatives through effective internal collaboration and engagement with external stakeholders. 


Job Purpose: 


To provide high-quality administrative and operational support to the Product and Regional Development Wild Atlantic Way team, enabling the effective and timely delivery of programme initiatives, destination and experience development plans, stakeholder engagement, product development and cross-functional projects that maximise the region’s potential as a tourism destination. 


Primary Objectives/Key Responsibilities 


Programme and Destination Development Support 

  • Support implementation of Product and Regional Development Wild Atlantic Way programme initiatives in line with agreed project plans, timelines and team KPIs. 
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of Destination and Experience Development Plans. 
  • Support new and existing product development and related communications. 
  • Contribute to Product and Regional Development Wild Atlantic Way media and trade familiarisation trips and itineraries. 
  • Assist with the coordination and delivery of marketing campaigns (e.g. shoots, content creation, etc) and projects, including taking individual responsibility for managing specific elements of campaigns, collaborating both with the wider team and also under own initiative. 

 

Stakeholder and Cross-Functional Collaboration 

  • Work closely with other Fáilte Ireland divisions to support the delivery of cross-functional projects. 
  • Assist in managing relationships and communications with tourism businesses and external stakeholders. 
  • Attend trade and stakeholder events and provide timely follow-up arising from meetings, workshops and engagements. 

 

Meetings, Events and Communications 

  • Assist with the organisation, delivery and follow-up of meetings, workshops and events. 
  • Provide logistics support, including issuing invitations, arranging venues and room layouts, booking accommodation, organising payments and liaising with invitees. 
  • Create and deliver presentations for meetings and events. 
  • Record, produce and distribute accurate minutes and agreed follow-up actions. 

 

Systems, Administration and Governance 

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date information in the Trade Engagement Database (TED) and Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system, including marketing lists. 
  • Provide day-to-day administrative support to the local Wild Atlantic Way team. 
  • Support the team in reporting on data, learnings and ROI analysis  
  • Support the coordination and preparation of content/presentations for projects, marketing and/or internal and external meetings as required. 
  • Ensure activities are delivered on time, within budget and in accordance with Fáilte Ireland finance processes. 
  • Ensure any third-party procurement is undertaken in line with Fáilte Ireland procurement policy. 

 

Carry out all other duties as required and participate as a full member of the Product and Regional Development Wild Atlantic Way team by supporting other work and projects as required from time to time. 


Person Specification: 


The successful candidate will be an organised and proactive administrator with strong office-management, marketing, communication and interpersonal skills. They will be able to prioritise competing demands, meet deadlines and work effectively in a busy team environment. They will communicate clearly in writing and orally, collaborate confidently with colleagues and external stakeholders, and demonstrate accuracy and attention to detail when coordinating activities, maintaining systems and preparing materials.


This role requires travel and attendance at a number of national and regional locations and sites each year. The working pattern is Monday to Thursday. The flexibility to work unsociable hours may be required.  


Essential Criteria:

In order to be eligible to apply for this role you must have / demonstrate in your application form the following:


  • A minimum of two years’ experience in an administrative and marketing role, including experience working in a busy administrative environment. 
  • A professional qualification at a minimum of Level 6 on the QQI Framework in a related discipline. 
  • A high level of proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint.  
  • Experience in budget administration and diary management. 


Desirable Requirements:


  • Previous experience in the tourism industry. 
  • Experience using CRM systems and internal software packages. 
  • Proficiency in the Irish language  


Key Competencies


  • Planning & Managing Work 
  • Managing Relationships 
  • Communicating Effectively 
  • Teamwork 


Office Location and Blended Working:

We do not ask for addresses as part of the application process, however it is the responsibility of the candidate to acknowledge the base location of the role. The successful candidate must regularly work from and attend the base office location of the role.

 

Please note: Remote working from outside the State is not permitted other than in exceptional circumstances. As this role is within the Irish public service, the post-holder must carry out a minimum of 80% of their working time within the State (Republic of Ireland). Candidates who reside in Northern Ireland must be able to meet this requirement.

 

  • This role requires travel, with attendance at a number of national and regional locations / sites on an annual basis.
  • The working pattern is Monday to Thursday


Blended working model, with an office location in Galway, Sligo, Cork or Killarney 

 

The current vacancy is based out of Galway or Sligo 

A panel will also be established from this competition to fill future vacancies that may arise in Cork or Killarney. 

 

Selection Process: 

Shortlisting will be based on applications and the selection process may involve two competency based interviews. A panel of successful candidates may be formed following the selection process.

 

Interview Attendance Requirement: 

Candidates must be available to attend an in-person interview at the location and date specified by Fáilte Ireland. Please note that the location of the interview may vary from the base location of the role.


Salary and Benefits

 

€43,071–€64,166*.

*This role will be filled in line with Public Pay Policy at Point 1 of the relevant Salary Scale unless the successful candidate is appointed from an existing public sector role.


The Annual Leave allowance for this post is 23 days.


Further details on the benefits on offer can be found in the Why Work with Fáilte Ireland? | Fáilte Ireland · Failte Ireland

Role Purpose – About the Opportunity

The Commission for Railway Regulation (CRR) is seeking a motivated and capable individual to join its Cybersecurity, Critical Infrastructure and Artificial Intelligence (CCIAI) Division as an Inspector.

This is an opportunity to contribute to an important and developing area of regulation, helping to strengthen cybersecurity, critical infrastructure resilience and the responsible use of artificial intelligence across Ireland's rail and cableway sectors.

We welcome applications from candidates with experience in regulation, governance, risk management, compliance, audit, information technology, public administration, project delivery or related fields.

You do not need to be an expert in all these areas to apply. We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate sound judgement, strong organisational and analytical skills, clear communication and a willingness to develop their expertise.


What You Will Be Doing

1. Regulatory Oversight and Compliance

  • Support inspections, audits, compliance reviews and supervisory activities.
  • Help develop risk-based approaches to regulation under NIS2, CER and the AI Act.
  • Review evidence and contribute to regulatory findings and recommendations.
  • Assist with incident notifications and associated regulatory responses.
  • Monitor emerging cybersecurity, resilience and technology-related risks.

2. Policy, Procedures and Continuous Improvement

  • Develop and maintain regulatory policies, guidance and procedures.
  • Support case management, incident handling and regulatory coordination.
  • Identify opportunities to improve internal systems and processes.
  • Contribute to digitisation and organisational improvement.
  • Support divisional planning, reporting and governance activities.

3. Communication and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Prepare reports, briefings, guidance and recommendations.
  • Build relationships with regulated organisations, public bodies and industry representatives.
  • Coordinate stakeholder meetings and communications.
  • Provide guidance to stakeholders in line with agreed CRR positions.

4. National and European Collaboration

  • Support CRR participation in national and European regulatory forums.
  • Prepare briefings and coordinate follow-up actions.
  • Exchange knowledge and best practice with other regulatory authorities.
  • Contribute to a consistent and effective regulatory approach.

Your Initial Priorities

During the initial period, you will focus on four key areas:

  1. Developing regulatory approaches: Supporting the introduction of risk-based inspection and supervision arrangements for cybersecurity and critical infrastructure resilience.
  2. Establishing effective procedures: Helping develop processes for case management, incident notifications, regulatory coordination and record keeping.
  3. Supporting stakeholder engagement: Preparing clear guidance, briefings and communications.
  4. Building regulatory relationships: Supporting engagement with national and European authorities.

Specialist knowledge of the relevant regulatory frameworks will be developed further through experience in the role.


Who We Are Looking For

We are looking for someone who can work independently, exercise sound judgement, communicate clearly and contribute positively to a developing regulatory function.

You may have developed these skills through the public or private sector, including regulation, governance, compliance, risk management, audit, operations, IT, project management or related professional environments.

We particularly value candidates who can:

  • Analyse information and make evidence-based decisions.
  • Organise priorities and deliver high-quality work.
  • Communicate complex information clearly.
  • Build productive working relationships.
  • Take ownership of responsibilities and demonstrate initiative.
  • Adapt to new challenges and develop specialist knowledge.


Essential Eligibility and Selection Criteria


1. Qualifications

A minimum Level 8 qualification on the National Framework of Qualifications (NFQ) in a relevant discipline.

Relevant disciplines may include engineering, information technology, cybersecurity, risk management, audit, compliance, governance, regulation, public administration or a related field.


2. Professional Experience

Relevant professional experience in one or more of the following, or a comparable environment:

  • Regulation, public administration or public service delivery.
  • Governance, risk management, compliance or audit.
  • Information technology, operational or technical functions.
  • Project delivery, policy development or stakeholder engagement.

Previous experience in the rail sector is not essential.


3. Core Skills and Capabilities

Candidates must demonstrate:

  • Judgement and analysis: Ability to assess information, evaluate evidence and reach reasoned conclusions.
  • Organisation and delivery: Strong planning, prioritisation and time management skills.
  • Communication: Ability to prepare clear reports, briefings and recommendations.
  • Relationship management: Ability to work effectively with colleagues and external stakeholders.
  • Regulatory and technical understanding: Knowledge of public administration, regulation, governance, compliance or risk management, and the ability to understand relevant technical and operational issues.
  • Review and assessment skills: Experience supporting reviews, audits, assessments, evidence gathering or similar activities.
  • Adaptability and initiative: Ability to work independently and develop expertise in new areas.


4. Other Requirements

  • Medical fitness for rail access, where required.
  • A full, clean Category B driving licence, or an undertaking to obtain one within the first year of appointment.


Desirable Experience and Qualifications

The following would be advantageous but are not essential to apply.

Regulatory, Risk and Assurance Experience

  • Experience in regulation, audit, compliance, risk management or operational oversight.
  • Experience in transport, infrastructure, utilities or other regulated sectors.
  • Involvement in inspections, investigations, compliance reviews or risk assessments.
  • Experience applying governance, risk or regulatory frameworks.

Technical and Sector Knowledge

  • Knowledge of cybersecurity, IT, operational resilience, operational technology, digital governance or artificial intelligence.
  • Familiarity with rail, public transport, critical infrastructure or other regulated environments.
  • Knowledge of relevant EU legislation or experience working with regulatory authorities.

Reporting and Professional Development

  • Experience preparing reports, recommendations or decision papers for senior management.
  • A relevant postgraduate qualification, recognised professional certification or substantial specialist training.

Your application must be submitted on the https://consciatalent.com/CRR website not later than 12 noon (Irish time) on Friday 20th November 2026.

Role Purpose

The Commission for Railway Regulation (CRR) is seeking an experienced and motivated professional to join its Cybersecurity, Critical Infrastructure and Artificial Intelligence (CCIAI) Division as a Senior Inspector (Grade I).

This is an opportunity to take on a senior role in an important and developing area of regulation, helping to shape how cybersecurity, critical infrastructure resilience and artificial intelligence are regulated across Ireland's rail and cableway sectors.

As Senior Inspector, you will play a key role in developing the division's regulatory approach, leading and coordinating regulatory activities, supporting colleagues and building relationships with regulated organisations and national and European authorities.

We welcome applications from experienced professionals with backgrounds in cybersecurity, governance, risk management, compliance, audit, assurance, regulation, information systems or related technical and operational fields.

Previous experience in the rail sector is not essential. We are particularly interested in candidates who combine sound professional judgement, analytical ability, organisational skills and leadership capability with an understanding of cybersecurity, risk and regulatory oversight.


What You Will Be Doing

The role combines regulatory leadership, technical oversight, stakeholder engagement and organisational development.

1. Lead Regulatory Oversight and Compliance

  • Plan, coordinate and deliver risk-based inspection, supervision, audit and compliance programmes.
  • Assess regulatory compliance and support proportionate, evidence-based regulatory decisions.
  • Lead and contribute to reviews of cybersecurity, organisational resilience and technology-related risks.
  • Oversee incident notifications and coordinate appropriate regulatory responses.
  • Monitor emerging risks affecting rail and cableway operations, including operational technology, networked systems and artificial intelligence.

2. Develop Regulatory Policies and Procedures

  • Contribute to the establishment and ongoing development of the CCIAI Division.
  • Develop and implement practical regulatory policies, guidance and operational procedures.
  • Establish effective processes for inspections, case management, incident handling, escalation and reporting.
  • Support the division's regulatory work programme and strategic priorities.
  • Identify opportunities to improve internal systems, processes and operational efficiency.
  • Contribute to digitisation, corporate governance and continuous improvement.

3. Provide Leadership and Support to Colleagues

  • Provide technical guidance and support to Engineer Grade 2 staff.
  • Coordinate workloads, priorities and regulatory activities.
  • Support colleagues in developing their technical and professional capabilities.
  • Promote collaboration, knowledge sharing and consistent working practices.
  • Contribute to effective team planning and operational management.

4. Build Relationships and Represent the CRR

  • Develop relationships with regulated entities, government departments, public bodies and industry stakeholders.
  • Lead stakeholder engagement, meetings and regulatory communications.
  • Prepare reports, briefings, guidance, recommendations and decision papers.
  • Represent the CRR at national competent authority groups and relevant European and international forums.
  • Collaborate with regulatory counterparts to share knowledge and promote effective regulatory approaches.


Your Initial Priorities

During the initial period in the role, you will focus on four key areas:

  1. Developing regulatory programmes: Establishing proportionate, risk-based inspection and supervision arrangements for cybersecurity and critical infrastructure resilience.
  2. Building effective operational processes: Developing procedures for case management, incident notifications, reporting, escalation and workflow coordination.
  3. Supporting and developing the team: Providing technical guidance, coordinating priorities and supporting professional development.
  4. Strengthening regulatory engagement: Building relationships with regulated organisations and national and European regulatory authorities.

The role offers scope to develop further specialist expertise while contributing to the direction and effectiveness of the division.


Who We Are Looking For

We are looking for an experienced professional who can take responsibility for complex work, provide leadership and contribute to the development of an effective regulatory function.

You may have developed your experience in the public or private sector, including cybersecurity, risk management, governance, audit, compliance, assurance, regulation, information technology or other technical and operational environments.

We particularly value candidates who can:

  • Lead and deliver: Take ownership of complex activities, manage priorities and achieve high-quality outcomes.
  • Exercise sound judgement: Assess technical and regulatory information, evaluate risks and make evidence-based recommendations.
  • Communicate effectively: Explain complex issues clearly and prepare high-quality reports and guidance.
  • Support and develop others: Provide direction, share expertise and contribute to an effective team.
  • Build strong relationships: Engage confidently with colleagues, regulated entities and external authorities.
  • Drive improvement: Identify opportunities to strengthen systems, processes and regulatory practices.
  • Adapt and develop: Apply existing expertise to evolving regulatory challenges.


Essential Eligibility and Selection Criteria

To be considered for this role, candidates must demonstrate the following.

1. Qualifications

A third-level or professional qualification at Level 8 or higher on the National Framework of Qualifications (NFQ) in a discipline relevant to the role.

Relevant disciplines may include cybersecurity, information systems, engineering, risk management, governance, compliance or a related field.

2. Professional Experience

A minimum of three years' relevant professional experience, preferably gained after qualification, in one or more of the following areas:

  • Cybersecurity governance or information security.
  • Risk management, compliance or regulatory oversight.
  • Audit, assurance or structured assessment activities.
  • Comparable technical, operational or regulated environments.

Candidates should demonstrate strong operational and organisational skills and the ability to deliver complex work.

Previous experience in the rail sector is not essential. Relevant experience gained in other regulated, technical or risk-based environments is welcomed.

3. Core Skills and Capabilities

Candidates must demonstrate:

  • Cybersecurity and risk expertise: In-depth knowledge of cybersecurity regulations, frameworks and good practice relevant to critical infrastructure and digital resilience.
  • Regulatory understanding: A strong understanding of public-sector legislation, regulation, governance and compliance, including the ability to develop knowledge of the CRR's statutory functions.
  • Leadership and management: Ability to lead, coordinate and develop a team, plan workloads and support professional development.
  • Analysis and judgement: Ability to evaluate complex information, identify risks and develop evidence-based recommendations.
  • Audit and assessment experience: Experience conducting or supporting audits, compliance reviews, assessments or structured assurance activities.
  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including preparing reports, briefings and recommendations.
  • Stakeholder engagement: Ability to build effective relationships with colleagues, regulated organisations, public bodies and other stakeholders.
  • Planning and delivery: Proven ability to manage priorities and deliver outcomes to agreed deadlines in technical, regulated or risk-based environments.

4. Other Requirements

  • Medical fitness for rail access, where required.
  • Possession of a full, clean Category B driving licence.


Desirable Experience and Qualifications

The following would be advantageous but are not essential to apply.

Professional Qualifications and Development

  • Relevant professional certifications such as Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) or Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC).
  • Relevant postgraduate qualifications or specialist training.
  • Evidence of ongoing professional development in cybersecurity, risk, governance, compliance or related areas.

Regulatory, Audit and Risk Experience

  • Experience leading or supporting security audits, risk assessments, compliance reporting or assurance programmes.
  • Experience in lead auditing, IT governance or organisational resilience.
  • Experience working within transport, infrastructure, utilities or other regulated or high-risk sectors.

Technical and Analytical Knowledge

  • Knowledge of operational technology (OT), industrial control systems or other critical infrastructure technologies.
  • Experience assessing complex cybersecurity, resilience or regulatory risks.
  • Strong analytical and decision-making skills, including interpreting technical information and developing practical recommendations.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

Cuspóir an Phoist 

Is iad an Ghaeltacht agus na hoileáin amach ón gcósta na háiteanna is suntasaí ar Shlí an Atlantaigh Fhiáin. Is áiteanna iad seo ina mhaireann an Ghaeilge seachas í a bheith ar taispeáint amháin; áiteanna ina bhfeidhmíonn pobail mar chaomhnóirí ar chultúr agus a dtagann cuairteoirí ó gach cearn den domhan chun taithí a fháil uirthi; agus áiteanna inar féidir leis an turasóireacht — má dhéantar i gceart í — a bheith ina fíorfhórsa do mharthanas agus muinín na bpobal sin. Tá Oifigeach á earcú ag Fáilte Ireland chun cabhrú leis é seo a bhaint amach. 

Is post nua tiomnaithe é seo le sainchúram a chuimsíonn na ceantair Ghaeltachta agus na hoileáin áitrithe feadh Shlí an Atlantaigh Fhiáin ar fad, ó Dhún na nGall go hIarthar Chorcaí. Agus é ag obair laistigh d’fhoireann Shlí an Atlantaigh Fhiáin agus in éineacht leis na hOifigigh Bhainisteoirí agus Tionscadal réigiúnacha, beidh an t-iarrthóir rathúil i gceannas ar fhorbairt eispéiris do chuairteoirí atá barántúil, in-díolta agus bunaithe ar an nGaeilge; feidhmeoidh an duine seo mar phríomhnasc leibhéal oibre Fáilte Ireland le hÚdarás na Gaeltachta agus leis na comhlachtaí stáit eile atá gníomhach sna réimsí seo; agus beidh sé/sí ina g(h)uth poiblí muiníneach, dátheangach le haghaidh na hoibre seo sna meáin agus sa Ghaeltacht. Is ról é seo do dhuine a bhraitheann chomh compordach céanna i halla pobail oíche Mháirt agus a bhraitheann sé/sí i seomra boird gníomhaireachta maidin Dé Céadaoin, duine atá in ann smaointe a thiontú ina dtáirgí ar féidir le gnólachtaí iad a dhíol agus go gcuimhneoidh cuairteoirí orthu. 

Is ról é seo a éilíonn Gaeilge líofa, saineolas i bhforbairt táirgí nó eispéiris turasóireachta, bainistíocht caidrimh den scoth ar fud comhlachtaí poiblí agus pobail, taithí ar fhlaithiúlacht, agus ní mór cur chuige cruthaitheach, praiticiúil a bheith aige/aici chun rudaí a chur i gcrích. Tá sé dírithe ar thionscnaimh a sheachadadh chun: 

  • An Ghaeltacht agus na hoileáin a fhorbairt mar shnáithe comhleanúnach, ardcháilíochta agus iomaíoch go hidirnáisiúnta de thairiscint cuairteoirí Shlí an Atlantaigh Fhiáin. 
  • An Ghaeilge a shuíomh mar eispéireas beo, inrochtana do chuairteoirí, ní mar dhéantán oidhreachta. 
  • Fáilte Ireland, Údarás na Gaeltachta agus gníomhaireachtaí stáit eile a ailíniú ionas go mbeidh infheistíocht phoiblí sna ceantair seo ag freastail don phobal. 
  • Cumas gnólachtaí Gaeltachta agus oileánda, grúpaí pobail agus eagraíochtaí ceann scríbe a fhorbairt, a chur i láthair agus a dhíol. 


Cur Síos ar an bPost 


Forbairt Táirgí & Eispéireas – An Ghaeltacht agus na hOileáin 

  • Ceannaireacht a thabhairt maidir le heispéiris nua agus fheabhsaithe do chuairteoirí a aithint, a dhearadh agus a sheachadadh ar fud na Gaeltachta agus na n-oileán ina bhfuil cónaí orthu, le béim ar leith ar eispéiris ar féidir a dhíol, ar féidir a chur in áirithe i nGaeilge agus ar eispéiris a bhaineann le cultúr maireachtála. 
  • Na gníomhartha a bhaineann leis an nGaeltacht, leis an nGaeilge agus le na hoileáin a chur i bhfeidhm laistigh de na Pleananna Forbartha Eispéiris Cinn Scríbe (DEDPanna), ag obair go dlúth le na Bainisteoirí réigiúnacha agus le na hOifigigh Tionscadail a bhfuil gach ceann scríbe acu. 
  • Smaointeoireacht chruthaitheach, fianaisebhunaithe a thabhairt d’fhorbairt táirgí: Bearnaí a aithint, coincheapa a thástáil le pobail agus leis an tionscal, agus smaointe a fhorbairt ina dtionscadail atá incháilithe do mhaoiniú agus indéanta a chur i gcrích. 
  • Léiriú cultúrtha, treoshuíomh cuairteoirí agus ábhar a fhorbairt a thugann barántúlacht agus muinín don Ghaeltacht agus do na hoileáin sa dá theanga. 
  • Tacú le forbairt turasóireachta na n-oileán, lena n-áirítear an turas cuairteora ó mhórthír go hoileán, tosaíochtaí bonneagair mara agus rochtana, maoirseacht cuairteoirí agus inbhuanaitheacht. 
  • Oibriú le feidhmeanna Margaíochta, Digiteacha, Forbartha Tionscail agus Infheistíochta Fháilte Ireland chun a chinntiú go ndéantar táirge Gaeltachta agus oileáin a ghabháil, a chur chun cinn agus a thacú trí chláir chorparáideacha; achoimrí tionscadail, cásanna gnó agus tuarascálacha ar dhul chun cinn a ullmhú de réir mar is gá. 


Bainistíocht Páirtithe Leasmhara & Comhoibriú Idirghníomhaireachta 

  • Gníomhú mar chaidreamh oibre laethúil Fháilte Ireland le hÚdarás na Gaeltachta, ag tacú leis an gcomhpháirtíocht straitéiseach idir an dá ghníomhaireacht agus ag cinntiú go ndéantar comhthionscnaimh a phleanáil, a chur ar fáil agus a sheachadadh ar amlínte comhaontaithe. 
  • Caidrimh tháirgiúla a chruthú le na Ranna atá freagrach as an nGaeltacht agus as na hoileáin, Comhdháil Oileáin na hÉireann, údaráis áitiúla, Turasóireacht Éireann, grúpaí LEADER agus comhlachtaí poiblí eile atá gníomhach sna ceantair seo. 
  • Dul i mbun rannpháirtíochta le heagraíochtaí pobail Gaeltachta agus oileánda, comharchumann, oifigigh pleanála teanga, Eagraíochtaí Bainistíochta Cheann Scríbe agus gnólachtaí turasóireachta chun ceannach isteach agus comhúinéireacht tosaíochtaí a chinntiú. 
  • Ullmhú agus tacú le struchtúir rialachais idirghníomhaireachta (grúpaí stiúrtha, grúpaí oibre); ionadaíocht a dhéanamh ar son Fáilte Ireland ar ardáin chomhoibríocha chomhaontaithe; saincheisteanna suntasacha straitéiseacha a chur faoi bhráid an Bhainisteora le hanailís shoiléir agus roghanna molta. 
  • Tacú le hiarratasóirí Gaeltachta agus oileánda chun dul i ngleic le cláir infheistíochta caipitil agus maoinithe oibriúcháin Fháilte Ireland agus chun iarratais láidre a ullmhú. 


An Ghaeilge, na Meáin agus an Chumarsáid 

  • Feidhmiú mar urlabhraí dátheangach do Fháilte Ireland ar chúrsaí turasóireachta Gaeltachta agus oileánda, ag tabhairt faoi agallaimh leis na meáin chumarsáide go líofa i nGaeilge agus i mBéarla ar fud an raidió, ar an teilifís, i gcló agus go digiteach. 
  • Coimrí, cur i láthair agus ábhar scríofa a fhorbairt ar ardchaighdeán sa dá theanga, agus cur i láthair agus ceardlanna i nGaeilge agus i mBéarla a chur ar fáil do lucht féachana pobail, tionscail, gníomhaireachta agus corparáideacha. 
  • Tacú leis an eagraíocht a cuid dualgas faoi Achtanna na dTeangacha Oifigiúla a chomhlíonadh i leith gníomhaíochtaí turasóireachta Gaeltachta agus Gaeilge, agus comhairle a chur ar chomhghleacaithe maidir le húsáid mhuiníneach na Gaeilge in ábhar atá dírithe ar chuairteoirí. 


Cumas Tionscail & Pobail 

  • Tacaíochtaí uasoiliúna, meantóireacht agus cruthú ábhair do ghnóthaí Gaeltachta agus oileánda a chomhordú, a sheachadtar trí Ghaeilge nuair is cuí. 
  • Oibriú le EBCSanna ar an gcósta Gaeltachta agus ar na hoileáin agus le heagraíochtaí pobail chun a rialachas, a dtairiscint ballraíochta agus a gcumas digiteach a neartú, agus chun dea-chleachtas a roinnt ar fud Shlí an Atlantaigh Fhiáin. 
  • Oibriú thar theorainneacha Gaeltachta ina n-éilíonn geilleagar na gcuairteoirí é. Is annamh a bhíonn pobail Ghaeltachta ina gceann scríbe féinchuimsitheacha: d’fhéadfadh an bonn cóiríochta, príomh-nithe is díol spéise, mol iompair nó baile tairsí a bheith suite lasmuigh de cheantar na Gaeltachta. Forbróidh an tOifigeach táirge agus comhpháirtíochtaí a nascann na ceantair chomharsanachta seo leis an tairiscint Ghaeltachta, lena chinntiú go dtreorófar cuairteoirí a mhealltar chuig ceann acu chuig an gceann eile, agus go rachaidh an tairbhe chun sochair do phobail na Gaeltachta. 

 

Oibríochtúil, Rialachas & Corparáideach 

  • Ardchaighdeáin a leabú i bpleanáil agus seachadadh tionscadal; buiséid shannta a bhainistiú; a chinntiú go ndéantar na gníomhaíochtaí go léir a sheachadadh in am agus de réir buiséid, agus go gcomhlíonann gach soláthar beartas Fháilte Ireland, oibleagáidí caiteachais phoiblí agus riachtanais Státchabhrach. 
  • Monatóireacht a dhéanamh ar dhul chun cinn i gcoinne pleananna, PTFanna agus rioscaí agus tuairisciú go rialta don Bhainisteoir; a chinntiú go bhfuil an ghníomhaíocht ar fad ailínithe le beartas náisiúnta turasóireachta, leis an Straitéis Forbartha Turasóireachta Réigiúnacha agus le straitéis Shlí an Atlantaigh Fhiáin. 
  • Léirigh luachanna corparáideacha Fáilte Ireland agus páirt a ghlacadh mar bhall iomlán d’fhoireann Shlí an Atlantaigh Fhiáin, ag tacú le tionscadail eile ó am go chéile agus ag comhlíonadh aon dualgas eile de réir mar a shannfar iad. 
  • An Ghaeilge a chur chun cinn laistigh d’Fháilte Ireland féin. Oibriú le foirne inmheánacha ar fud na heagraíochta chun úsáid laethúil na Gaeilge a spreagadh agus a normalú, tionscnaimh chruthaitheacha a eagrú (mar shampla gníomhaíocht Sheachtain na Gaeilge, ciorcail chomhrá, píolótaí ábhair dátheangacha nó taispeántais foirne) agus rannpháirtíocht i gcláir foghlama, uasoiliúna agus feasachta Gaeilge a spreagadh, ionas go mbeidh muinín na heagraíochta sa Ghaeilge ag teacht leis an uaillmhian atá aici don Ghaeltacht. 

 

Éilíonn an ról seo taisteal nach beag ar fud na Gaeltachta agus pobail oileán ar Shlí an Atlantaigh Fhiáin, ó Dhún na nGall go hIarthar Chorcaí, lena n-áirítear tréimhsí rialta thar oíche agus taisteal farantóireachta chuig oileáin amach ón gcósta, agus freastal ar láithreacha náisiúnta agus réigiúnacha. Beidh uaireanta oibre neamhshóisialta i gceist leis, lena n-áirítear tráthnónta, deireadh seachtaine agus, go minic, laethanta saoire bainc. Gné den ról seo is ea solúbthacht chun taisteal sa bhaile agus, uaireanta, go hidirnáisiúnta. 


Sonraíocht an Duine 

Critéir Riachtanacha 

  • Gaeilge líofa, labhartha agus scríofa, agus an cumas gnó, cur i láthair agus agallaimh leis na meáin a dhéanamh go muiníneach trí Ghaeilge. 
  • Cumarsáidí den scoth, le scileanna idirphearsanta dea-fhorbartha agus cumas léirithe chun muinín a chothú le pobail, gnólachtaí agus comhlachtaí poiblí araon. 
  • Saineolas láidir sa smaointeoireacht chruthaitheach, le cuntas teiste maidir le smaointe a ghiniúint agus iad a iompar ó choincheap go seachadadh. 
  • Cumas léirithe chun caidrimh a bhainistiú le páirtithe leasmhara iolracha a mbíonn cuspóirí agus spreagthaí éagsúla acu go minic, agus torthaí a sheachadadh do chách. 
  • Tuiscint phraiticiúil ar phobail Ghaeltachta agus/nó oileáin agus na deiseanna agus íogaireachtaí a bhaineann le forbairt turasóireachta sna háiteanna sin. 
  • Breithiúnas fónta, athléimneacht agus an cumas ionadaíocht inchreidte a dhéanamh ar an eagraíocht go poiblí. 
  • Toilteanas agus cumas taisteal suntasach a dhéanamh, lena n-áirítear chuig oileáin amach ón gcósta, agus oibriú lasmuigh d’uaireanta caighdeánacha. 


Chun a bheith incháilithe chun iarratas a dhéanamh ar an ról seo, ní mór duit an méid seo a leanas a bheith agat / a léiriú i d’fhoirm iarratais: 

  • Taithí trí bliana ar a laghad i ról ábhartha (e.g. turasóireacht, forbairt ceann scríbe nó eispéiris, forbairt chultúrtha, phobail, forbairt Ghaeilge nó eacnamaíochta, nó cumarsáid). 
  • Líofacht sa Ghaeilge agus sa Bhéarla. 
  • Taithí i mbainistíocht agus pleanáil tionscadail. 
  • Taithí i mbainistíocht páirtithe leasmhara, lena n-áirítear le comhlachtaí poiblí nó le gníomhaireachtaí stáit. 
  • Taithí ar chur i láthair do pháirtithe leasmhara inmheánacha/seachtracha. 
  • Modh iompair féin acu agus ceadúnas tiomána iomlán;  
  • Inniúlacht i Microsoft Office. 


Cáilíochtaí / Oiliúint Éigeantach 

  • Tá cáilíocht ghairmiúil (ar a laghad Leibhéal 6 faoin gCreat QQI) i ndisciplín ghaolmhar riachtanach. 


Critéir Inmhianaithe 

  • Taithí ar agallaimh leis na meáin nó ar chumarsáid phoiblí i nGaeilge agus i mBéarla. 
  • Taithí dhíreach ag obair le nó i gcomhar le hÚdarás na Gaeltachta, comharchumainn na nOileán, Comharchumainn nó comhlachtaí Gaeltachta oileánda eile. 
  • Teist cruthaithe i bhforbairt táirgí turasóireachta, eispéireas nó ceann scríbe, agus eolas oibre ar cheantair Ghaeltachta agus oileáin Shlí an Atlantaigh Fhiáin. 
  • Taithí oibre san earnáil fáilteachais 
  • Taithí ar oibriú le heagraíochtaí pobail, comharchumainn nó Eagraíochtaí Bainistíochta Ceann Scríbe. 
  • Taithí ar bhainistíocht buiséid, soláthair nó riarachán deontas i gcomhthéacs na hearnála poiblí. 
  • Tuiscint ar Achtanna na dTeangacha Oifigiúla agus ar phleanáil teanga. 


Príomhinniúlachtaí 

Caidrimh a Bhainistiú: Inis dúinn faoi thráth ar oibrigh tú i gcomhar le páirtithe leasmhara éagsúla a raibh tosaíochtaí nó cuspóirí difriúla acu, amhail comhlachtaí poiblí, eagraíochtaí pobail agus gnólachtaí. Conas a chruthaigh tú tacaíocht, conas a bhainistigh tú na leasanna éagsúla agus conas a d’oibrigh tú i dtreo toradh comhaontaithe? 

 

 Cumarsáid Éifeachtach: Inis dúinn faoi am nuair a rinne tú ionadaíocht ar d’eagraíocht agus go raibh ort faisnéis a chur in iúl do raon páirtithe leasmhara nó lucht éisteachta seachtrach. Conas a chuir tú do chumarsáid in oiriúint don lucht éisteachta agus cén toradh a bhí air? 

 

Ag Glacadh le Nuálaíocht: Inis dúinn faoi am inar shainaithin tú deis chun táirge, eispéireas cuairteora, seirbhís nó tionscnamh eile a fhorbairt nó a fheabhsú. Cén chaoi ar fhorbair tú an smaoineamh agus ar thástáil tú é, conas a chuaigh tú i ngleic le daoine eile sa phróiseas agus conas a thóg tú é ón gcoincheap go dtí an seachadadh? 

 

Inis dúinn faoi smaoineamh bunaidh a mhol tú chun rud éigin nua a chruthú nó chun cur chuige difriúil a ghlacadh, cibé acu is táirge, eispéireas cuairteora, seirbhís nó modh oibre é. Cén áit ar tháinig an smaoineamh sin as? cén fáth a raibh sé difriúil ón méid a bhí ann cheana féin, agus conas a chuir tú ina luí ar dhaoine eile tacú leis? Cad a tharla, agus cad a dhéanfá ar bhealach difriúil? 

 

Obair a Phleanáil agus a Bhainistiú: Inis dúinn faoi thionscadal nó faoi thionscnamh a raibh tú freagrach as a phleanáil agus a sheachadadh lena mbaineann gníomhaíochtaí nó páirtithe leasmhara iolracha. Conas a bhunaigh tú an plean, a ndearna tú bainistiú ar thosaíochtaí agus acmhainní, conas a rinne tú monatóireacht ar dhul chun cinn agus conas a thug tú aghaidh ar rioscaí nó saincheisteanna chun seachadadh rathúil a chinntiú? 

 

 

Suíomh Oifige agus Obair Chumaisc 

Ní iarraimid seoltaí mar chuid den phróiseas iarratais; mar sin féin, tá sé de fhreagracht ar an iarrthóir aitheantas a thabhairt do bhunshuíomh an róil. Ní mór don iarrthóir rathúil oibriú go rialta ó shuíomh na bunoifige an róil agus freastal air. Ní cheadaítear cianobair ó lasmuigh den Stát seachas i gcúinsí eisceachtúla. Ós rud é go bhfuil an ról seo laistigh de sheirbhís phoiblí na hÉireann, ní mór do shealbhóir an phoist 80% ar a laghad dá gcuid ama oibre a dhéanamh laistigh den Stát (Poblacht na hÉireann). Ní mór d’iarrthóirí a bhfuil cónaí orthu i dTuaisceart Éireann a bheith in ann an riachtanas seo a chomhlíonadh. 


Próiseas Roghnúcháin 

Beidh an gearrliostú bunaithe ar iarratais agus d’fhéadfadh dhá agallamh bunaithe ar inniúlacht a bheith i gceist leis an bpróiseas roghnúcháin. Déanfar agallaimh trí Ghaeilge go páirteach, agus d’fhéadfaí iarraidh ar iarrthóirí measúnú gearr Gaeilge a dhéanamh, a bhféadfadh agallamh meán ionsamhlaithe a bheith i gceist leis. Féadfar painéal d’iarrthóirí rathúla a bhunú tar éis an phróisis roghnúcháin. Ní mór d’iarrthóirí a bheith ar fáil chun freastal ar agallamh pearsanta ag an suíomh agus ag an dáta atá sonraithe ag Fáilte Ireland; d’fhéadfadh suíomh an agallaimh a bheith éagsúil ó shuíomh bunaidh an róil. 

 

Is fostóir comhdheiseanna é Fáilte Ireland agus tá sé tiomanta d’ionad oibre cuimsitheach a chothú a bhfuil meas aige ar éagsúlacht an lucht saothair agus a bhaineann leas as an éagsúlacht sin. Molaimid duit teagmháil dhíreach a dhéanamh linn ag recruitment@failteireland.ie má theastaíonn cúnamh nó cóiríocht réasúnta uait le linn an phróisis earcaíochta. 

 

Conas Iarratas a Dhéanamh

job.title: Officer Product and Regional Development, Ireland’s Ancient East
job.description:
Key Details:

 

Location: Cork 

*The current vacancy is based in Cork.  

A panel will also be established from this competition to fill future vacancies that may arise in Dublin, Mullingar or Waterford. 

Contract: Full-time, Permanent

Salary: €58,528 – €83,697 (starting at the first point of the scale)

Closing date: Thursday, 12 November 2026 at 3pm


Application Form: Failte Ireland_Officer, Product and Regional Development Ireland's Ancient East _Application Form.docx


Fáilte Ireland invites applications for the position of Officer, Ireland’s Ancient East. The role will report to a Manager Product and Regional Development. At a destination level, the successful candidate will be responsible for delivering projects which help deliver on the objectives of the Ireland’s Ancient East Regional Tourism Development Strategy and associated local Destination and Experience Development Plan. 


Job Purpose: 


The role will deliver manage product development investment projects and destination development projects to drive increased tourism revenue and seasonal extension The successful candidate will also manage local stakeholders and support tourism enterprises in their development.   

 

Primary Objectives/Key Responsibilities 


Destination and Experience Development Plan (DEDP) Delivery 

  • Implementation of Destination and Experience Development Plans (DEDPs) across the Ireland’s Ancient region to deliver on objectives set out in the Fáilte Ireland Corporate Strategy and Ireland’s Ancient East Regional Tourism Development Strategy at a local level. 
  • Translate key strategic development priorities for the Ireland’s Ancient East into actionable plans and deliverables at destination level to drive sustainable economic growth. 
  • Coordinate project activities, timelines and stakeholder inputs, monitor milestones and escalate risks. 
  • Contribute to the completion of needs analysis and implement activity to develop the destination and drive visitor appeal according to relevant market segments. 
  • Support visitor experiences to seek innovative approaches to leverage opportunities, adapting to changing market conditions. 


Investment Programme & Scheme Delivery  

  • Support the rollout of Fáilte Ireland investment schemes and identify projects that meet regional objectives. 
  • Manage multiple investment projects including management of cash flow, drawdown deadlines and navigate an effective path to deliver agreed KPIs. 

 

Stakeholder Engagement  

  • Maintain relationships with tourism businesses and public stakeholders. 
  • Deliver development programmes to industry clusters and networks to drive regional growth 
  • Develop and harness industry and destination networks to actively collaborate to gain buy-in and commitment on project priorities and areas of focus.
  • Identify themes and experiences and work with stakeholders and businesses (both individually and through clusters/networks) to develop & enhance their tourism offering. 
  • Ensure communication internally and externally is consistent, timely and relevant. 


Corporate Programme Delivery 

  • Coordinate with colleagues across Fáilte Ireland functions to help align experience development, industry development, and marketing and sales activation at destination level, in line with identified destination needs. 
  • Contribute to programme delivery plans by identifying regional needs and opportunities, tracking uptake and spend, and supporting outcome reporting. 


Governance & Reporting  

  • Comply with all relevant organisational policies, procedures and governance requirements in the delivery of assigned work. 
  • Monitor progress against assigned tasks, plans and timelines, highlighting risks, issues or delays to the relevant manager in a timely manner. 
  • Prepare accurate updates, information, reports or analysis as required to support decision-making, planning and delivery within the area. 
  • Apply agreed processes for risk, budget, procurement, expenditure and records management within the scope of the role. 
  • Use relevant data, evidence and insights to support planning, reporting, evaluation and continuous improvement. 
  • Ensure assigned programme, project or operational activity is delivered in line with Fáilte Ireland policy, public sector obligations and delegated authority. 

 

Carry out all other duties as required and participate as a full member of the Ireland’s Ancient East team by supporting other work and projects as required from time to time. 

 

Please note that travel is required as part of this role. Flexible working hours may also be a requirement, as the job requires working outside 9-5 at times. 


Person Specification: 


  • Applicants must meet the essential criteria and demonstrate, through relevant examples in their application, the key competencies outlined below. 


Essential Criteria:

In order to be eligible to apply for this role you must have / demonstrate in your application form the following:


  • A minimum of three years’ relevant professional experience in destination development, investment programme management, tourism development, or a related area.
  • Experience in commercial decision making based on insight and metrics
  • Experience in managing multiple complex stakeholders to reach consensus
  • Experience in managing multiple complex work programmes while working on projects led by others
  • Experience in translating organisational strategy into delivery projects
  • Access to own means of transport/valid driving licence (Regular travel is required as a core part of the role within the region and throughout Ireland)
  • A professional qualification (min level 6 under the QQI framework) in a related discipline  


Desirable Requirements:


  • Experience in tourism experience development, destination development or investment in tourism product


Key Competencies


  • Commercial Awareness 
  • Managing Relationships 
  • Planning and Managing Work 
  • Strategic Thinking 


Office Location and Blended Working:

We do not ask for addresses as part of the application process, however it is the responsibility of the candidate to acknowledge the base location of the role. The successful candidate must regularly work from and attend the base office location of the role.

 

Please note: Remote working from outside the State is not permitted other than in exceptional circumstances. As this role is within the Irish public service, the post-holder must carry out a minimum of 80% of their working time within the State (Republic of Ireland). Candidates who reside in Northern Ireland must be able to meet this requirement.

 

  • This role requires travel, with attendance at a number of national and regional locations / sites on an annual basis.
  • Flexible working hours may also be a requirement, as the job requires working outside 9-5 at times. 

 

Selection Process: 

Shortlisting will be based on applications and the selection process may involve two competency based interviews. A panel of successful candidates may be formed following the selection process.

 

Interview Attendance Requirement: 

Candidates must be available to attend an in-person interview at the location and date specified by Fáilte Ireland. Please note that the location of the interview may vary from the base location of the role.


Salary and Benefits

 

€58,528 – €83,697*.

*This role will be filled in line with Public Pay Policy at Point 1 of the relevant Salary Scale unless the successful candidate is appointed from an existing public sector role.


The Annual Leave allowance for this post is 27 days.


Further details on the benefits on offer can be found in the Why Work with Fáilte Ireland? | Fáilte Ireland · Failte Ireland


How to Apply


Conscia will be managing all aspects of the recruitment process on behalf of Fáilte Ireland

On this page, you can click on and download the Application form below:


Application Form: Failte Ireland_Officer, Product and Regional Development Ireland's Ancient East _Application Form.docx


Applications for this role are ONLY accepted on submission of a completed Application Form, available to download directly above.


You can also submit your completed Application Form by clicking "Apply for Job". Please note that CVs and Cover Letters should not be submitted. No enquiries or canvassing may be made to Fáilte Ireland.

 

The closing date for receipt of completed applications is Thursday, 12th November 2026 at 3pm (Irish time). Applications will not be accepted after this deadline. Late applications will be ineligible for consideration. Therefore, it is your responsibility to ensure that you have allowed sufficient time for transmission of your application.

 

An acknowledgment email will be issued in respect of all applications received (this email will acknowledge receipt and it will not confirm eligibility or otherwise).


If an applicant does not receive an acknowledgement email within two working days of the date of submission, the applicant should contact failte@consciatalent.com to ensure the application has been received.

job.title: Legal Officer, Licensing (Administrative Officer - Standard Scale)
job.description:
GRAI Candidate Information Booklet - Legal Officer, Licensing (AO Standard Scale).Final.pdf


GRAI Application Form - Legal Officer, Licensing (Administrative Officer, Standard Scale) - Final.docx


The Role:

The GRAI is seeking to appoint a Legal Officer, Licensing (Administrative Officer - Standard Scale.) Successful applicants will be placed on a panel for a period of up to 18 months to fill future vacancies for a Legal Officer, Licensing (Administrative Officer - Standard Scale) or similar roles within GRAI.


Applications must be made by attaching a completed application form via the Conscia website which can be downloaded below.


Overview:

Reporting to the Assistant Director of Licensing (Legal), the Legal Officer - Licensing, (AO - Standard Scale) will be a critical role responsible for ensuring that gambling operators applying for licenses have appropriate corporate structures in place, that the gambling operators satisfy the (i) Legal and Corporate (ii) Account Officer and (iii) Premises Assessment Frameworks. The successful candidate will ensure that all the application documentation comply with the Gambling Regulation Act and associated regulations. 


Supporting the Assistant Director of Licensing - Legal (AP), the successful candidate will review the suitability and viability of applicants, ensuring adherence to relevant legal standards and regulations. This role requires a thorough understanding of legal structures and regulatory compliance.

The role will involve providing legal advice, opinion and interpretation of the Gambling Regulation Act 2024 and  secondary legislation. This is an excellent opportunity to join a newly established regulator and contribute to the  effective, consistent and legally robust assessment of applications, supporting GRAI in carrying out its statutory responsibilities.


Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

• Provide high quality, clear and timely legal advice on aspects of the GRAI’s licensing functions as provided for, in the Gambling Regulation Act 2024.

Formed in 2002, IN2 is a progressive engineering consultancy operating across Ireland, the UK, and Europe, dedicated to creating better spaces for people. With over 100 experts across six locations, our team of engineers, technicians, and consultants collaborate closely with clients and partners to deliver innovative, sustainable, and energy-efficient building solutions across a wide range of sectors—from concept and design through to handover and beyond.

At IN2, joining our team means being part of a collaborative, high-performing, and forward-thinking organisation, where your contribution makes a real impact—and where career opportunities grow alongside our business. 

 

Working Hours  

We operate a 37.5-hour working week designed to support work-life balance. We offer flexible start and finish times between 8am and 6pm, provided that core hours of 10am to 4pm are covered for team collaboration and meetings.  

 

About The Role

Athlone offers the chance to do career-defining work without long commutes or city pressure. You will be trusted, supported, and encouraged to shape how things are done locally, with full backing from the wider IN2 team.  As a Senior Electrical Engineer at our Athlone Office, you will:   

  • Assist senior engineers with project management, on-site inspections, technical surveys, and design team meetings 
  • Play an active role in project delivery from concept through to completion 
  • Support the management team in client relationships, budgeting, and reporting 
  • Contribute to mentoring junior staff, reviewing design work, and providing guidance 
  • Collaborate with senior engineers for ongoing mentorship and growth 


Your Experience 

To be considered for this role, you should have:  


Essential 

  • Degree in Building Services Engineering or Electrical Engineering 
  • Minimum of 4 years’ experience in electrical design, ideally within a consultancy environment 
  • Passion for career progression and aspiration to achieve Chartered status (if not already obtained) 


Why You’ll Love Being Part of the Team 

At IN2, we’ve traded the stuffy corporate ladder for a flat hierarchy and a culture where your voice actually matters. We’re a diverse, collaborative team that believes the best ideas can come from anyone, anywhere. 

  • Global Impact, Local Feel: You’ll get to work on game-changing projects across different countries, supported by our specialist BIM, Sustainability, and Building Physics teams. 
  • Constant Growth: Through IN2 Talks, cross-office collaboration, and a culture of knowledge sharing, you’re always learning something new. 
  • Your Best Self: We prioritise a genuine work-life balance with flexible hours and support for personal circumstances. We’re big on open communication and ensuring our workplace is a bias-free zone where you can truly be yourself. 


What’s In It For You? 

We’ve put together a package that looks after your wallet, your career, and your wellbeing. 


The Essentials 

  • Competitive Pay & Bonuses: A salary that reflects your worth, plus an annual bonus and pension contributions. 
  • Annual Leave: 22 days of annual leave, scaling up to 27 days as you grow with us (plus all those bank holidays!). 
  • Flexible Hours: Work-life balance isn't just a buzzword here—we offer a 37.5-hour working week with flexible hours (8am–6pm), to suit your lifestyle! 


Career Progression 

  • Personal Roadmap: You’ll have a dedicated Personal Development Plan and mentoring from our senior leaders. 
  • The IN2 Academy: Access to our internal academy, CPD support, and expert assistance in advancing your career,  

 

Health & Wellbeing 

  • Mind & Body: Access to our Employee Assistance Program, annual health checks, and various fitness initiatives. 
  • Commute Greener: Take advantage of our Cycle to Work scheme to keep active on your way to the office. 


Social & Community 

  • Legendary Events: From our famous Christmas party weekend to Employee Appreciation Day and regular staff social events. 
  • Giving Back: Get involved with our team-led charity initiatives. 
  • International Reach: opportunities to work across IN2 offices in London, Dublin, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone, and Madrid 


Eligibility: Due to regulatory requirements, this role is open to candidates with permanent residency or unrestricted right to work in Ireland only. Applications requiring visa sponsorship cannot be considered.
